summary.headline: GIC Re Q1 FY27 combined ratio improved to 104.88% from 106.94%, with PAT of INR1,922.04 crores and solvency at 4.32.
summary.overview: GIC Re reported Q1 FY27 gross premium of INR13,475.36 crores, up from INR12,388.01 crores a year earlier, and PAT of INR1,922.04 crores on PBT of INR2,490.25 crores. Incurred claim ratio fell to 85.04% from 90.42% and combined ratio improved to 104.88% from 106.94%. Investment income dipped to INR3,265.51 crores from INR3,313.74 crores. Management flagged soft global pricing, a provisional INR440 crores for the Gujarat floods, and continued pruning of the foreign book, which declined about 6% in the quarter.

vs INR3,313.74 crores in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR157,800 crores, of which equity about INR58,000 crores
financial_highlights.change: fixed income about 73.4%, equity about 17%, money market about 8.67%

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Domestic combined ratio was about 107.5% in Q1, versus the roughly 102-103% range management cited as typical; domestic motor deteriorated on legacy treaties. Growth was about 12.3%, led by non-property lines and retail health.

segments.name: Foreign / international
segments.commentary: Foreign book declined about 6% YoY; management is repricing motor, aviation and overseas cargo, with property the largest exposure. Overseas combined ratio improved sharply in Q1, but management said one quarter is not representative given seasonality.

segments.name: Life reinsurance
segments.commentary: Life book grew meaningfully and is held at about a 20% market share; management said the portfolio is still loss-making and should be judged over a cycle of a couple of years.

segments.name: Subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Consolidated profit fell versus standalone. AICL profit fell about 60%, South Africa posted a loss of INR287 crores and Moscow a loss of about INR29 crores in Q1.

guidance_outlook: Targets roughly 10% growth overall, with foreign growth expected to exceed domestic; mid-year review to revisit the target.
Combined ratio targets split by book: domestic about 103% (close to current levels) and foreign about 95%, expected in 2 to 3 years.
Maintain domestic market share despite competition; rebuild foreign business lost after the rating downgrade, while continuing pruning.
Long-term goal of 50:50 domestic-to-international mix; medium-term target 60:40. Management said it will not pursue these at the cost of risk-return.
A-rating upgrade (from A-) possible in about 4 to 5 years, subject to IFRS and RBC implementation and business position.
Management expects solvency to decline gradually as profitability improves and growth remains measured.
capex_capacity: No capacity or capex plans discussed on the call; the call covered reinsurance underwriting and investment book only.

Investment book: about INR120,000 crores at book value and INR157,000-157,800 crores at market value (equity about INR58,000 crores), as stated on the call. Management said the debt share is stable and equity will stay around 17%.
Major domestic reinsurance renewals occur on 1 April; management used reinsurance tools to support domestic insurers.
demand_pricing: Global reinsurance capacity is ample and pricing is soft; competitive behaviour is seen across most players, including Indian reinsurers, foreign branches and GIFT City entrants, especially in property cat.
Management said cat losses typically come to GIC at about 30-40% of market losses; flood claims for Gujarat are still developing.
IRDAI issued directives on 22 July 2026 on property rates quoted on the direct side, which management described as guidance whose impact will be seen over the next 2-3 quarters.
Health: growth driven by retail health rather than corporate or group health, which management views as more loss-prone. Obligatory share of domestic book was about 33% in Q1.
Foreign premium remains well below the roughly INR18,000 crores once reached; management expects recovery to take 3-4 years given softer rates.

qa_highlights.question: Which market players have been aggressive in pricing, and will the softness deepen given benign cat experience and Gujarat flood losses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said almost all players have been competitive given surplus global capacity. GIC's cat losses usually run at 30-40% of market losses, and flood claims are still developing, so the company is watching claims development before concluding.

qa_highlights.question: What changed in the overseas book to produce the strong Q1 overseas combined ratio, and is it structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Mokashi said the foreign book is being reviewed class by class, with action on motor, aviation and cargo, and property the largest exposure. One quarter may not be representative, there is seasonality, and some first-quarter accounting entries may affect the result. No number was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did domestic combined ratio deteriorate to about 107.5%, and what is the full-year view?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic motor deteriorated because of legacy treaties; competition is intense in property. Health growth is in retail rather than group. Management did not give a full-year domestic combined ratio and pointed to the 1 April renewals and reinsurance tools.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Gujarat flood provision in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: The company has provided INR440 crores in Q1 for the Gujarat flood event; the figure was restated several times on the call during the answer.

qa_highlights.question: Is the net worth excluding fair value falling from about INR51,000 crores to INR45,000 crores, and why is net worth including fair value flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would recheck the excluding-fair-value figure. For net worth including fair value, the flat trend is attributed to falls in equity market value, which offset profits; the CIO put the fair value reduction at about INR11,000-15,000 crores. Details were deferred to a later call.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline to reach a 103% domestic and 95% foreign combined ratio, and how does it relate to capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said domestic is fairly close to 103%, while the 95% foreign target is 2-3 years away. Solvency at 4.3 is seen as conservative during the post-downgrade recovery and the IFRS/RBC transition, and is expected to decline gradually.

risks_watch: Soft property cat pricing and aggressive competition from GIFT City and foreign players may erode margins.
Gujarat flood claims development beyond the INR440 crores provision.
Foreign book shrank about 6% and the combined ratio remains unproven beyond one quarter; overseas cargo, aviation and motor are under review.
Domestic motor and retail health loss ratios; domestic combined ratio about 107.5% in Q1.
Life reinsurance profitability, which management said is still under review over a cycle.
Subsidiary losses (South Africa INR287 crores, Moscow INR29 crores) and the AICL profit decline of about 60%.
Net worth including fair value flat over several years; the Q1 net worth decline is under reconciliation by management.
IFRS and RBC implementation, and the IRDAI property-rate directive.
summary.management_tone: Confident on underwriting and profitability, but cautious on growth and on the foreign book, which management described as still under repair. Management was evasive on timelines for the foreign turnaround and the full-year domestic combined ratio, and was unable to reconcile the net worth figure on the call.
key_quotes: We would like to have combined ratio target for domestic book at something like 103 and the foreign book at 95 in line with the global markets.
We do not want to grow at the cost of profitability.
Maybe not in a couple of years because of the significant softening trends, the same exposure is coming at a lesser premium.

growth.why: Management targets roughly 10% premium growth for FY27 (under mid-year review), with no specific capacity, orders or contracts quantified behind it; Q1 gross premium grew about 8.8% YoY and foreign book fell about 6%, while domestic grew about 12.3%.
